Action Plan:
1. Advised patient to proceed immediately to the nearest Emergency Department for assessment of new-onset shortness of breath and tachycardia 4 weeks post-C-section, with concern for possible pulmonary embolism (PE).  
2. Explained postpartum clot risk, possible need for blood tests (e.g., D-dimer), imaging (e.g., CTPA or V/Q scan), and anticoagulation if PE confirmed.  
3. Offered ambulance transfer; patient preferred self-transport. Instructed her to leave promptly and to call an ambulance if symptoms worsen en route.  
4. Advised to take essential items for the baby and to arrange partner support as soon as possible.  
5. Instructed patient to withhold further Codeine until evaluated.  
6. Recorded Ibuprofen allergy for hospital team.  
7. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Presenting complaint: Sudden shortness of breath for ~1 hour while sitting watching TV.  
• Associated symptoms: Dry cough since yesterday; sensation of rapid heartbeat; chest soreness on deep inspiration; C-section scar tenderness. No frank chest pain at rest; no sputum production.  
• Onset/progression: SOB acute onset, not previously experienced; symptoms perceived as stable but patient feels anxious.  
• Past obstetric history: Elective/emergency C-section 4 weeks ago; otherwise well.  
• Past medical history: Denies chronic medical conditions.  
• Medications: Codeine (dose/route/frequency not documented)—used regularly post-op, none taken in past week.  
• Allergies: Ibuprofen—reaction unspecified (patient unsure of details).  
• Family history: Mother with leg clots (deep-vein thrombosis).  
• Social: Caring for newborn at home; partner currently at work; no one else present.

Objective:
• Self-palpated pulse: 30 beats counted over timed interval (exact seconds not specified); clinician interpreted as “slightly fast.”  
• No other vitals or physical examination findings documented.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute shortness of breath 4 weeks postpartum  
   - Assessment: Suspected pulmonary embolism.  
   - Differential: Post-infective reactive airway disease, postpartum cardiomyopathy, pneumonia, anxiety.  
   - Investigations (ED): Vitals, ECG, full blood count, D-dimer, CXR, CTPA or V/Q scan.  
   - Treatment (ED): Oxygen as needed, anticoagulation if PE confirmed.  
   - Referral: Emergency Department immediately.

2. Postoperative pain control / Codeine use  
   - Assessment: Post-C-section pain currently mild; no analgesia for past week.  
   - Treatment: Withhold Codeine until hospital review; reassess need for alternative analgesia postpartum.

3. Ibuprofen allergy  
   - Assessment: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) allergy.  
   - Plan: Document clearly; avoid NSAIDs until full allergy details clarified.

Quality checks:
● Missing clinically expected elements: complete allergy reaction details; comprehensive current medication list; vital signs (BP, HR, RR, SpO₂, temperature); smoking/ETOH history.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; minor pauses but clinically adequate.
